title: Shanghai-Style Braised Pork Belly (Hong Shao Rou)
equipment: 14-inch wok with lid or 5-quart heavy pot with lid

items: 1½ lb lean skin-on pork belly, cut into ¾-inch-thick pieces
2 tbsp neutral oil, such as canola, vegetable or avocado
2 tbsp rock sugar or granulated sugar
2 to 3 cups water, for braising, plus more as needed

steps: Put the pork belly pieces in a 3-quart saucepan and add enough of the blanching water to cover. Bring to a boil over high heat and boil about 1 min, just until the pork looks opaque on the outside.
Drain the pork in a colander, rinse it under running water to wash off any scum, and set it aside. Discard the blanching water.
Add the oil and sugar to a clean wok or heavy pot over low heat. Stir until the sugar melts into a light amber syrup, 2 to 4 min. Watch it closely so it doesn't burn.
Add the pork and raise the heat to medium. Cook, stirring and turning the pieces, until they are lightly browned and coated in the caramel, 5 to 7 min.

Lower the heat to low and pour in the Shaoxing wine. Let it bubble for 2 min. Stir in the soy sauce, dark soy sauce and 2 cups of the braising water, adding up to 1 more cup if needed to nearly cover the pork.

Cover and simmer over medium heat for 45 min to 1 hr, until a fork slides easily through the pork. Stir every 5 to 10 min so nothing sticks, and add a splash more water whenever the pan starts to look dry. The pork will be well past the safe 145°F by now; check a thick piece with a thermometer if you like.

Once the pork is tender, uncover and look at the liquid. If a lot remains, turn the heat to high and stir constantly until the sauce cooks down to a thick, glossy coating on the pork, 3 to 8 min. Let it rest 3 min off the heat, then serve.
tips: Rock sugar gives the glossiest, most even glaze, but granulated sugar works fine.
Don't walk away during the final reduction. The sugary sauce goes from glossy to scorched fast.
Serve with steamed rice to soak up the sauce.
storage: Refrigerate in an airtight container up to 4 days or freeze up to 3 months. Thaw overnight in the fridge, then reheat in a covered pan over medium-low heat with a splash of water until hot throughout.
